title: Degree adverbs (B1)
note: very / really / quite / a bit · too vs enough · so vs such · absolutely + extreme adjectives · seeded from Martina's `not so much relaxing` 2026-08-16

cards.title: Stronger, weaker, softer
cards.body: Before an adjective you can set the volume: `really/very` (strong), `quite` (medium), `a bit` (soft, usually for negatives). The polite negative is `not very`: The hotel was not very clean. Czech `ne moc` maps to `not very` — never `not so much`.
cards.body_cz: Před přídavným jménem lze nastavit hlasitost: `really/very` (silné), `quite` (střední), `a bit` (jemné, obvykle pro zápor). Zdvořilý zápor je `not very`: The hotel was not very clean. České `ne moc` = `not very` — nikdy `not so much`.

cards.title: too and enough
cards.body: `too` + adjective = more than is good: too cold to swim. `enough` goes AFTER the adjective: big enough, warm enough. To strengthen `too`, use `far` or `way`: far too expensive.
cards.body_cz: `too` + přídavné jméno = víc, než je dobré: too cold to swim. `enough` stojí AŽ ZA přídavným jménem: big enough, warm enough. `too` se zesiluje pomocí `far`/`way`: far too expensive.

cards.title: so vs such · absolutely
cards.body: `so` + adjective/adverb: so windy, so well. `such` + (a) + noun phrase: such a windy day. Extreme adjectives (amazing, freezing, empty) refuse `very` — use `absolutely/completely/really`: absolutely amazing.
cards.body_cz: `so` + přídavné jméno/příslovce: so windy, so well. `such` + (a) + jmenná fráze: such a windy day. Extrémní přídavná jména (amazing, freezing, empty) odmítají `very` — patří k nim `absolutely/completely/really`: absolutely amazing.

items.en: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.cz: Moře bylo příliš studené na koupání.
items.gap: The sea was ____ cold to swim in.
accepts: The sea was too cold to swim in.
items.explanation: too = more than is good. `very cold` just describes; `too cold to swim` means swimming is off.
items.explanation_cz: too = víc, než je dobré. `very cold` jen popisuje; `too cold to swim` znamená, že koupání nepřipadá v úvahu.

items.en: Our room was not big enough for four people.
items.cz: Náš pokoj nebyl dost velký pro čtyři lidi.
items.gap: Our room was not big ____ for four people.
accepts: Our room was not big enough for four people.
items.explanation: enough comes AFTER the adjective: big enough, warm enough.
items.explanation_cz: enough stojí AŽ ZA přídavným jménem: big enough, warm enough.

items.en: It was so cold that we stayed inside.
items.cz: Bylo tak zima, že jsme zůstali uvnitř.
items.gap: It was ____ cold that we stayed inside.
accepts: It was so cold that we stayed inside.
items.explanation: so + adjective (+ that clause). `such` would need a noun.
items.explanation_cz: so + přídavné jméno (+ věta s that). `such` by potřebovalo podstatné jméno.

items.en: It was such a cold day that we stayed inside.
items.cz: Byl tak studený den, že jsme zůstali uvnitř.
items.gap: It was ____ a cold day that we stayed inside.
accepts: It was such a cold day that we stayed inside.
items.explanation: such + (a) + noun phrase: such a windy day. `so` pairs with a bare adjective.
items.explanation_cz: such + (a) + jmenná fráze: such a windy day. `so` se pojí jen s přídavným jménem.

items.en: The hotel was not very clean.
accepts: The hotel was not very clean.
items.explanation: The polite negative is not very + adjective. `not so much clean` is not English.
items.explanation_cz: Zdvořilý zápor je not very + přídavné jméno. `not so much clean` anglicky neexistuje.

items.en: The trip was not very relaxing.
accepts: The trip was not very relaxing.
items.explanation: Czech `ne moc` = not very. Not `not so much relaxing`.
items.explanation_cz: České `ne moc` = not very. Ne `not so much relaxing`.

items.en: The food was a bit too spicy for me.
items.cz: Jídlo pro mě bylo trochu moc pálivé.
items.gap: The food was a ____ too spicy for me.
accepts: The food was a bit too spicy for me.
items.explanation: a bit softens: a bit too spicy, a bit tired. `a little bit or more` does not scale.
items.explanation_cz: a bit zjemňuje: a bit too spicy, a bit tired. `a little bit or more` takhle nefunguje.

items.explanation: Extreme adjectives (amazing, freezing, exhausted) take absolutely/really, never very.
items.explanation_cz: Extrémní přídavná jména (amazing, freezing, exhausted) berou absolutely/really, nikdy very.

items.explanation: Ordinary (gradable) adjectives take very/really. `absolutely warm` does not work.
items.explanation_cz: Běžná (stupňovatelná) přídavná jména berou very/really. `absolutely warm` nefunguje.

items.en: We were quite tired after the walk.
items.cz: Byli jsme po té procházce docela unavení.
items.gap: We were ____ tired after the walk.
accepts: We were quite tired after the walk.

items.en: The tickets were far too expensive.
accepts: The tickets were far too expensive.
items.explanation: To strengthen too, use far/way: far too expensive. `very too` is impossible.
items.explanation_cz: Pro zesílení too se používá far/way: far too expensive. `very too` nejde.

items.en: She speaks English so well that people think she is British.
items.cz: Mluví anglicky tak dobře, že si lidé myslí, že je Britka.
items.gap: She speaks English ____ well that people think she is British.
accepts: She speaks English so well that people think she is British.
items.explanation: so + adverb (+ that clause): so well, so fast.
items.explanation_cz: so + příslovce (+ věta s that): so well, so fast.

items.en: It was quite a long journey.
accepts: It was quite a long journey.
items.explanation: quite comes BEFORE a/an: quite a long journey.
items.explanation_cz: quite stojí PŘED a/an: quite a long journey.

items.en: Is the room warm enough for you?
items.cz: Je ti v pokoji dost teplo?
items.gap: Is the room warm ____ for you?
accepts: Is the room warm enough for you?
items.explanation: enough after the adjective, in questions too.
items.explanation_cz: enough za přídavným jménem i v otázce.

items.en: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.cz: Počasí bylo na řízení extrémně náročné.
items.gap: The weather was ____ difficult for driving.
accepts: The weather was extremely difficult for driving.
items.explanation: extremely strengthens gradable adjectives: extremely difficult.
items.explanation_cz: extremely zesiluje stupňovatelná přídavná jména: extremely difficult.

items.en: The beach was completely empty in the morning.
items.gap: The beach was ____ empty in the morning.
accepts: The beach was completely empty in the morning.
items.explanation: Absolute adjectives (empty, full, impossible) take completely/absolutely, not very.
items.explanation_cz: Absolutní přídavná jména (empty, full, impossible) berou completely/absolutely, ne very.
